parts.part: whole town (mounds A-D and the western mound, Sukkur Industrial and Trading Estate)
parts.layout_phase: Mature Indus or Harappa phase (no layout phase defined by the excavators)
parts.what_was_built: The 2006 excavations by Shah Abdul Latif University, Khairpur, exposed 'complex residential structures, among which are burnt and mud brick walls, rooms, doors, platforms, roads, and the remains of a drainage system' (Shaikh, Veesar and Mallah 2004-2005, Ancient Sindh 8: 60, fig. 27; 96, pl. 92, as summarised by Biagi and Vidale 2022 pp. 5-6). The 1996 excavation of mound C is reported to have exposed 'walls, bathing platforms, covered drainage' (Shar and Shah 2022 p. 5). In the 2017 salvage trenches on the western mound the room walls were 'made from compact clay and not the normal mold made mud bricks', with steatite and faience workshops (Sindh Directorate of Antiquities). None of these sources describes a street grid, gives its extent or names the phase in which it was laid out.
parts.locator: biagi2022lakhan pp. 5-6 (citing Shaikh, Veesar and Mallah 2004-2005); kalich2022lakhan p. 5; sindhantiq_lakhian
parts.excavator_basis: Cross-dating of pottery and craft debris to the Harappa phase as dated at Harappa: 'it is clear that the site was occupied during the Harappa Phase as defined at the site of Harappa, which is well dated to around 2600-1900 BCE' (Sindh Directorate of Antiquities site page, on the 2013 and 2017 salvage excavations). The one radiocarbon date (below) comes from a 1996 test trench and is not tied to any structure.

radiocarbon.context: Mound D, Trench C (one of three parallel trenches about 3 x 1.5 m on the western slope, excavated by G. M. Shar in November 1996): a charcoal lens about 3 cm thick at 30 cm depth in the northern profile, with two potsherds, about 25 cm from a copper figurine; sampled January 1997
radiocarbon.phase: Mature Indus Civilization (excavators' attribution from pottery)
radiocarbon.calibrated_published: 2881-2133 cal. B.C. 2s [94.2%]; d13C -25.59 (as printed, with the minus sign in a symbol font)
radiocarbon.note: Measured at the Groningen Centre for Isotope Research. The paper does not state the half-life or the calibration curve; Groningen reports conventional ages, which by definition use the 5568-year half-life, but we leave the 5568 fields empty because the source does not say so. The date does not come from a structure of the town plan; it bears on the layout only as evidence that the Mature Indus occupation at mound D falls in the second half of the third millennium BC. Coordinating pass: the source does not print the half-life; the laboratory reports conventional radiocarbon ages (Stuiver and Polach 1977), so the printed age is copied to the 5568-year fields.

syntheses.statement: Biagi and Vidale write that the date 'attributes this part of the sequence to the Mature Indus Civilization, confirming the suggestion of the first excavators', and that earlier reports on comparable contexts 'apparently pointed to the mid-third millennium B.C.'; they describe it elsewhere as 'an associated ordinary radiocarbon date from charcoals of the mid-third millennium cal. B.C.' (p. 10).

syntheses.page: online summary of Biagi and Vidale 2022
syntheses.statement: Describes the Trench C charcoal as 'radiocarbon dated to roughly 2000 BCE'.
syntheses.disagreement: Rounds the date toward the end of the calibrated range; Biagi and Vidale give 2881-2133 cal B.C. and call it mid-third millennium.

parts.conflicts: No source we could read identifies a planned layout or a layout phase; the 'roads' and 'drainage system' of 2006 are known only from Biagi and Vidale's one-sentence summary of the unavailable Ancient Sindh report. The site's area is given as nearly 50 hectares by ul-Haq and Ali (2001, quoted by Biagi and Vidale p. 5), while Shar and Shah (2022 p. 3) call it the second largest city after Mohenjo-daro without a figure.

first_occupation.phase: Possible Early Harappan (Kot Diji) occupation in the lowest levels of a deep trench; claimed earlier ('Hakra' or Mehrgarh-like) pottery at the base
first_occupation.basis: Pottery only. The Sindh Directorate of Antiquities reports that 'in the lowest part of this deep excavation pottery that is similar to the Early Harappan, Kot Diji Phase has been recovered (Kenoyer 2000)' about two metres below the surface, and that further excavation is needed 'to determine if this is a chance discovery or if there is an Early Harappan occupation at the site'. Shar and Shah (2022 pp. 5-6) list a sequence of Late Indus on the surface, Mature Indus (Level I), Kot Dijian (Level II) and 'Hakra.Mehergarh' (Level III, an 'expert opinion' relating the lowest pottery to Mehrgarh), and report that the 2000 excavations were 'conducted to the water levels'. No date range is given for these levels.

notes: Lakhanjo-daro (also written Lakhan-jo-Daro, Lakheen-Jo-Daro, Lakhian-jo-Daro and Lakhueen-jo-Daro) lies under the industrial estate on the northern edge of Sukkur and has been dug only in small and salvage trenches by Shah Abdul Latif University, Khairpur, and the Sindh government between 1992 and 2017. The published record we could reach confirms Mature Indus houses, platforms, drains and 'roads' but no mapped street grid, so we cannot name a layout phase or say when one was laid out; the town entry records what is known so that a measurer's find can be placed in context. The only radiocarbon date is GrN-23123 from a 1996 test trench on mound D. The main excavation reports were not available to us: Shaikh, N., Veesar, G. M. and Mallah, Q. H. 2004-2005 (published 2006), Excavations of Indus period site Lakhan-Jo-Daro 2006, Ancient Sindh 8: 7-196; Mallah et al. 2012 on the 2009-10 season; Mallah 2017 on the 2017 salvage work; ul-Haq and Ali 2001 on the 1994 season (Museum Journal, National Museum of Pakistan); and Kazi 1985 and 1989. We searched for these by title on the web and found only citations. The KALICH article's lists of seasons and levels are informal and partly second-hand ('the relative chronology was verbal discussed with excavator').
